title: Operate-or-Outsource Inference Playbook
content:
Purpose:
Quick, pragmatic messaging & battle-test notes for sales/solutions on "operate vs outsource" decisions for customers evaluating vLLM/TGI/TensorRT-LLM style self-hosted stacks vs Redwood Managed/Dedicated/Private. Emphasis: operator effort, unseen recurring costs, day-2 reliability, and SLO-driven tradeoffs.

Audience:
- AE/SE pre-sales and solutions engineers
- GTM content writers and battlecard owners
- Product marketing working on competitive position

TL;DR position (one line):
Many teams can run a proof-of-concept with open stacks in weeks; keeping it cost-effective, reliable, and safe at production scale is an operations problem that compounds — Redwood turns unpredictable operational cost and availability into predictable SLOs and clear unit economics.

Core messaging pillars (short bullets for decks/email):
- Time-to-reliable: POC ≠ production. Self-hosted gets models running fast; maintaining latency P95/99, autoscale, and fallbacks costs weeks/months of ops work.
- Hidden operator tax: recurring effort for quantization regressions, kernel mismatches, upstream model changes, and KV-cache correctness. Each incident is developer time + business cost.
- Economics of scale: GPU utilization, multi-tenant isolation, and batching decisions change with load. Small mistakes can 2–3x token cost.
- Compatibility & portability: Model pins, compiler/kernels (TensorRT) and toolchain drift make rollouts brittle. Redwood abstracts those differences.
- Security & compliance: Private deployments and KMS/HSM integrations are non-trivial; we offer validated pathways and audits.

Competitive snapshot (notes to SEs, do not read verbatim in customer calls):
- vLLM: best-in-class for flexible batching/KV cache experimentation and fast iteration. Great for prototyping. Fragile for multi-tenant production unless you invest in robust autoscaling + preemption + tracing.
- TGI (Text Generation Inference): strong Apache ecosystem, good for teams that want containerized stacks and integration with Triton. Operationally heavy around model packaging and Windows/Linux kernel mismatches.
- TensorRT-LLM / TRT fused runtimes: high throughput/lowest latency on supported hardware, but high fragility when model architecture or quantization changes; engineering cost to recompile/validate kernels per model.

Common buyer profiles & recommended playbook:
- Early-stage AI-native (seed/Series A): care about speed/cost. Pitch Redwood Hosted for fast time-to-value; offer migration path to Dedicated later. Emphasize free credits + benchmarks.
- Product teams at scale (growth/scale stage): more sensitive to latency SLOs and cost predictability. Lead with Redwood Dedicated and cost-savings case studies (actual numbers).
- Regulated (enterprise/finance/healthcare): focus on Private + audit/KMS + proven SOC/ISO controls; highlight proven integrations and runbook automation.

Objections (real) and rebuttals (field-tested):
- "We can save money running ourselves."
  Rebuttal: show 12–18 month TCO with operator hours, incident MTTR, model regression rework. Use our unit-econ template (link in linked_artifacts) to walk through expected token costs vs ops tax.
- "We need full control over stack (for compliance/model changes)."
  Rebuttal: Redwood Private offers customer-managed networking and model pinning. Emphasize audit trail + deterministic rollout policies.
- "Open-source stacks are flexible; vendor lock-in is a risk."
  Rebuttal: Redwood supports open-models and exposes model variant compatibility; we avoid lock-in by standardizing APIs, and offer exportable configs and manifest-based rollbacks.

Operator-effort scorecard (short rubric for discovery calls):
- Initial POC time (days): vLLM 1–7, TGI 3–10, TRT-LLM 7–30 (depends on infra)
- Day-2 daily ops (hours/wk): small workload: vLLM 10–25h/wk, TGI 8–20h/wk, TRT-LLM 15–40h/wk
- Incident MTTR risk: vLLM medium, TGI medium, TRT-LLM high (compilation/kernels)
- When to recommend Redwood: if customer values < 1% token cost variance target, SLO-backed latency, or expects multi-region scale.

Narrative examples (talking points and 2–3 line hooks):
- For AEs: "We help you get past the false finish line of POC. Teams get a prototype quickly, but it's the next 6–12 months of brittle rollouts and unexpected GPU spend that break timelines — Redwood fixes that."
- For SEs: "We instrument at the token level and make batching/caching decisions observable and actionable — you can actually target per-route cost budgets without blind optimizations."
- For product: "Customers who tried to DIY often rebuild features we provide: prefix caching, seamless fallbacks, canary rollouts across model variants, and SLO-first autoscale policies."

Quantitative examples to use in discovery (replace with customer metrics):
- Case A (SaaS search): self-hosted team reported 2.3x higher per-1M tokens cost after accounting for idle GPU, preemption, and engineering time; Redwood Dedicated delivered equivalent latency at 0.8x token cost with 99.9% uptime SLA.
- Case B (regulated fintech): 4 weeks to stand up an on-prem prototype, 10 weeks to achieve compliant key management, 3 incidents tied to quantization regressions in the next quarter. Redwood Private shortened compliance runbook integration to 2 weeks with our partner playbook.

Sales tactics and experiments to run (growth):
- Offer a "Day-2 Ops" workshop: 2–4 hour working session with prospects to map their runbook and estimate ops tax. Convert high-estimate accounts to proof-of-value for Dedicated trials.
- Quick calc tool: build a one-page spreadsheet for AEs to input token volumes, p95 targets, and team hourly rates to estimate 12-month TCO.
- Run an inbound nurture with content: "Three hidden costs of running your own inference" with short checklist and sample mitigation plan.

Next steps / action items (who/what/when):
- [AE Playbook] Finalize a one-pager with the operator-effort scorecard for SDR/AE by 2024-07-05 (owner: Miguel Soto).
- [SE Collateral] Create a short demo script showing rollback from Quantized-8 to FP16 and the time/cost delta (owner: Avery Chen) - target 2024-07-19.
- [PM/Product] Track three customer migrations where the initial POC was self-hosted and they moved to Redwood; gather anonymous cost/time datapoints (owner: Priya Kapoor) - ongoing, present QBR.

Open questions / research items:
- Need more precise industry avg for day-2 ops hours per 100 QPS across vLLM/TGI/TRT — ask bench team to run synthetic 100QPS scenario and capture operator tasks/time.
- Quantify frequency of quantization-induced regressions per model type (LLAMA2, MPT, Falcon) in community deployments.

Notes to self / call-outs:
- Keep examples concrete and numeric. Buyers push back on vague "lower ops cost" claims.
- Emphasize rollback, tracing, and model compatibility in all enterprise conversations.
- Link to internal benchmark reports in collateral (see linked_artifacts).
